title: PG-19.3 Shared pure replay of a project's event log for the project store and the read-only reader (memev)
request: Programme contract PG-19.3 in memev: one shared, pure replay of a project's event log, so that the project store and the read-only reader of PG-19.2 cannot drift. Proposed and unsigned; the signer signs it after the red-team gate. It is version 3 of PG-19 and does not supersede PG-19.2: it changes the body of the reader that PG-19.2 specified and keeps every criterion of PG-19.2. Why: the project store replays its log in ProjectStore#_replay and #_applyRecord (src/engine/project-store.mjs), and Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, added by pull request #365 (PG-19.2, signed), replays the same log by a copy of those rules, because the reader must not open the store (opening it rewrites every snapshot, cuts a torn last line and takes no lock, which beside a live daemon changes files and can cut a line the daemon is still writing). The two are held together only by tests: the review of #365 found three places where the reader's replay differed from the store's, and its description names this contract as the follow-up. This contract makes the replay one pure function in a new module with no import, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, and moves both callers onto it. ORDER AND BASE: pull request #365 lands first, with its duplicate replay and its stronger agreement test (decided at its review). This contract is signed and built after #365 has merged, and it is the side that adapts: the store and the reader move onto the shared function, #365 changes nothing. The base recorded here, origin/main af8c6d7, is the commit this spec was written against and does not yet hold #365 (Vault#tasksReader, src/cli/work-store.mjs, test/cli-work.test.mjs and test/cli-work-e2e.test.mjs are all absent from it); the criteria that name them are written for the base the signer records, which must be a commit that holds #365, and a signature on an older base would make them red for the wrong reason. Code is named by symbol, never by line, because the line numbers of #365 move when it is pushed again. What the shared function keeps: it reads and reports only. The truncation of a torn last line, the rewrite of snapshots, the lock and the migration stay in the store; the function has a truncate option, on for the store and off for the reader, that decides only whether it reports the cut for the caller to make. An unterminated last line is never applied by either caller, as the store does today. Both callers refuse a schema version above the supported one with future_schema; a project at an older version needs_migration for the reader and is migrated by the store; a project with a meta.json and no log gives an empty reader; an unknown project gives null. The reader's surface is unchanged and stays silent: a frozen object with one member, snapshot(kind), also frozen, returning structuredClone copies, needing a read credential, with no way to reach the store, and no notice on it. The shared function returns the notices; where they show is left to a later spec. The reader is a point-in-time view: it replays once when Vault#tasksReader() is called, snapshot(kind) returns structuredClone copies of that state, it is not live, and the work command is one-shot (WP19-05 AC09). Four deviations from the store as it is today are made on purpose and stated, each one its own named criterion with its own assertion-based red test, so that a reviewer can sign or strike each separately (WP19-04 AC12 to AC15 for the function, WP19-05 AC03, AC04, AC07 and AC10 for the callers). The replay function fixes both store bugs it found rather than preserving them, and it never rewrites the log. DEVIATION A, the byte cut: the torn last line is cut at a byte offset and not at a character index. This changes what the store writes to a log on disk. Before, a log with a multi-byte character ahead of the torn line is cut inside a complete record and left corrupt (measured on this base: a log with accented and CJK text and a torn tail is 843 bytes before open and 791 after, and the log then holds a line that no longer parses). After, only the torn tail goes. The cut is made by the store, outside the shared function, and whether the store should keep cutting at all or stop rewriting the log is put to the red-team in the pull request. DEVIATION B: a line that is JSON but not a record (null and the like) is refused with a fixed refusal code, non_record_line, and never throws; today it throws on open. DEVIATION C: a schema version that is not a whole number is refused by both callers with bad_schema_version, where the store today opens it. DEVIATION D: an unreadable line in the middle of the log is refused with unreadable_middle_line; today the store skips it and keeps the records after it, so one existing block of test/project-store.test.mjs is replaced by the assertion of the refusal if this deviation is signed, and the contract is otherwise unchanged by striking it. A torn or unreadable final line, including invalid UTF-8 or JSON at the end of the file, is skipped and reported by a notice, as the store does today, and never applied when it has no newline. Claim E owns the build of PG-19.3 (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, the build-layer claim that also holds PG-19.2); the claim row is for the signer to add and is not part of this spec. Depends on contracts: PG-19.2 (Vault#tasksReader and the work port; its pull request #365 must have merged), SO-1.01 (requirement 3: only the vault, the coordinator and the project store name the store; test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs is not changed), SO-F-02 (the approval conflict rule that stays in project-store.mjs). Boundaries: PG-19.2 owns the facade, src/cli/work-store.mjs and the e2e test, and none of them changes here; a later reader that serves view('task') and conflicts() will also call the shared function and has its own contract, out of scope here; a lock-free read mode that opens the store is out of scope unless a later contract adds one with a proof, on disk beside a live daemon, that it changes nothing; PG-W-21A and PG-W-21B and anything in trust governance (ADR 8) are not touched. Wording of the refusals: the codes future_schema, needs_migration and bad_schema_version are pinned, and so are two phrases of the needs_migration message (the remedy, any daemon command that opens the store migrates it, and that this reader writes nothing), by regular expression, not the whole sentence, which is as of commit 094970a of pull request #365 (red at 58b4e97). Mutants: the table in WP19-04 AC11 maps one to one onto the 15 mutants of the red-team review of pull request #365 (M1 to M15, ids kept), each with its equivalent in the shared module or in the reader's wrapper and the test that must kill it. M1 to M9 are also killed by golden tests on the pure function alone (WP19-04 AC16 to AC24), each with a fixed log text and a literal expected state, so that the agreement of the reader and the store, which two equally wrong implementations would pass, is not the only test of them. Tests are written first and committed alone, every red on an assertion, with the new module imported dynamically inside a try. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository and is reached only across the WO-05-A call-out boundary (never vendored, no memev-merge); tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.title: One pure shared replay of a project's event log, src/engine/project-replay.mjs: state by kind and id, the store's replacement semantics, the unterminated last line, malformed lines, one refusal policy and fixed notice and refusal ids, with no import
requirements: SR-1.15: no code without a caller. The shared function has two callers in this contract, the store (WP19-05) and the vault's reader (WP19-05); neither is optional (source: docs/scope-one/WBS.md leaf 2.2.15; owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

one new module, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, holds the replay of a project's event log as one pure function, so that the project store and the read-only reader cannot drift. It exports exactly these names and no other: REPLAY_NOTICES, REPLAY_REFUSALS, APPROVAL_DECISIONS, unusableApproval, createReplayState, applyRecord, replayLog, schemaVerdict. It has no import at all (the allow-list of static imports is empty), so that it also loads from a copy for a mutation run. It is a module of its own, not part of project-store.mjs, for three reasons: project-store.mjs imports fs, which a pure function cannot; a module that names ProjectStore, projectStore(, coordinator( or new Coordinator would break requirement 3 of SO-1.01 (the regex /ProjectStore|projectStore\(|\bcoordinator\(|new Coordinator/ of test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs lets only coordinator.mjs, project-store.mjs and vault.mjs match it), so the shared module must not match it; and WP19-01 of PG-19.2 keeps src/cli/work-store.mjs free of ProjectStore, projectStore, project-store and Coordinator, so the reader's port never reaches the store, and a shared module named project-replay.mjs keeps that grep true (source: the replay it extracts from, ProjectStore#_replay and ProjectStore#_applyRecord in src/engine/project-store.mjs, and the second copy of it in Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, added by pull request #365, PG-19.2, signed)

replayLog(log, { truncate = false } = {}) takes the event log, as one string or as the file's bytes (a Uint8Array, which is what both callers pass, so that invalid UTF-8 is seen and not turned into replacement characters), the JSON Lines of the file in file order, and returns a new state { entities, seq, generation, usedIds, eventKeys, sources, approvals, hlc, notices, cut, refusal }: entities is a Map of kind to a Map of id to data; seq and generation are numbers; usedIds is a Set of record ids and entity ids; eventKeys is a Map of idempotency key to the last record that carried it; sources is a Map of 'kind:id' to { id, ts, seq } of the record that last wrote it; approvals is a Map of the id of the log event to { event, id, data }; hlc is the highest well-formed hybrid clock string seen, or null; notices is a list of { code, ... } with code in REPLAY_NOTICES; cut is null or { keep_bytes, dropped_bytes }; refusal is null or { code, line, message } with code in REPLAY_REFUSALS and line the 1-based number of the line that caused it. When refusal is not null the log is refused as a whole: the function stops at that line and returns the empty state with that refusal, nothing applied and nothing cut, and the callers throw it; the function itself never throws. createReplayState() returns the empty state (seq 0, generation 0, hlc null, nothing in any collection, notices [], cut null, refusal null). applyRecord(state, rec) applies one parsed record to state in place, returns state, and does not change rec. replayLog is createReplayState followed by applyRecord for each line, in line order (source: ProjectStore#_replay and ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs)

replacement keeps the store's semantics: a record is applied in file order, whatever its seq, hlc or gen say; a later write of the same kind and id replaces the data wholesale and never merges, the position of the id in its kind is where it first appeared, and sources names the later record; no record is ever removed: every record id stays in usedIds and every approval event stays in approvals even when two events carry the same approval id ('every approval write is its own event: a later write with the same id replaces the entity, never the event'); a record whose entity data is null leaves the id with a null value (a tombstone is the null, not a deletion); a kind that no store declares is kept as it arrived, and the callers decide what they serve (source: ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs; PG-19.2 reader)

bookkeeping and refusal: for every well-formed record, refused or not, a string id is added to usedIds, a well-formed hlc (the pattern of parseHlc in src/engine/oplog.mjs: 13 digits, a dot, 4 or more digits) that is higher than state.hlc replaces it, and seq becomes the larger of seq and the record's seq when that is a finite number. A refused record (refused is truthy) then stops: it adds no entity, no key, no source, no approval and no generation. Any other well-formed record sets generation to the larger of generation and (its gen when a finite number, else 0) plus 1, with or without an entity, and an idempotency key (a non-empty string) is kept in eventKeys. The shared function never decides to refuse a write: it only reads what the log holds (source: ProjectStore#_applyRecord in project-store.mjs)

lines: blank lines are skipped without a notice. The last non-blank line is the final line; every other non-blank line is a middle line. A line is unreadable when its bytes are not valid UTF-8 or its text is not valid JSON. (1) A final line with no newline after it is never applied, readable or not, and gives the notice torn_last_line (next requirement). (2) A final line that ends in a newline and is unreadable is skipped with the notice unreadable_last_line and its line number, and is neither cut nor changed. (3) DEVIATION D (its own criterion, WP19-04 AC15, so that it can be signed or struck alone): an unreadable middle line refuses the whole log with the refusal unreadable_middle_line and its line number. Before: the store skips such a line, reports it as 'events.jsonl: unreadable record skipped' and keeps the records after it (the block 'a bad line in the middle is skipped and reported, later records kept' of test/project-store.test.mjs). After: the log is refused, nothing is applied, and both callers throw the refusal; a torn line in the middle is the sign of a log damaged or edited somewhere other than at its tail, and serving the records around it would hide that. (4) DEVIATION B (its own criterion, WP19-04 AC13): a terminated line that parses to something that is not a plain object (null, a number, a string, an array, a boolean) refuses the log with the refusal non_record_line and its line number and never throws; before, a line of null throws on open in the store and in the reader of pull request #365. A record that is a plain object whose entity is present but is not a plain object, or has a kind or an id that is not a non-empty string, and is not refused, is applied not at all (no bookkeeping, no generation) with the notice malformed_record; before, the store keeps an entity with no id under the key 'undefined'; this part belongs to deviation B. Nothing here throws: every fault ends as a notice or a refusal (source: ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs; the position of the red-team review; a deviation from the store, stated)

the unterminated last line: a final segment with no newline after it, whether it is half a record, a whole valid record, invalid JSON or invalid UTF-8, is never applied by any caller, as the store does today; it is skipped in both modes and gives the notice torn_last_line with dropped_bytes, its UTF-8 byte length, because the shared function returns the notices (the reader drops them, see WP19-05). Only with truncate true (the store) does the state also carry cut { keep_bytes, dropped_bytes }, the byte length of the complete part and of the dropped part, so that the store can cut the file at keep_bytes; with truncate false (the reader) cut is null, because the reader never writes and another process may be in the middle of that line. The function itself never writes anything and never rewrites the log. DEVIATION A (its own criterion, WP19-04 AC12 here and WP19-05 AC03 in the callers): cutting the torn last line at a byte offset. This changes what the store writes to a log on disk. Before: ProjectStore#_replay finds the end of the complete part as a character index of the decoded text and passes that index to fs.truncateSync, which takes a byte length; with any multi-byte character before the torn line the index is smaller than the byte length of the complete part, so the file is cut inside a complete record and the log is left corrupt (measured on the base this spec was written against: a log with accented and CJK text and a torn tail is 843 bytes before open and 791 after, and the log then holds a line that no longer parses). After: the store cuts the file at cut.keep_bytes, so every complete line is kept byte for byte and only the torn tail is dropped; for an all-ASCII log nothing differs. The cut stays in the store, outside the shared function, as its own criterion; whether the store should keep cutting at all, or stop rewriting the log, is put to the red-team in the pull request (source: ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs; a deviation from the store, stated)

approvals: an approval record whose data cannot be used by the conflict rule (a decision outside APPROVAL_DECISIONS, or a resolves that is not a list of event ids, as unusableApproval says) is kept as an entity, stays out of approvals, and gives a notice 'approval_unusable' with the event id and the reason; the reason text is the text the store reports today. unusableApproval and APPROVAL_DECISIONS move here from project-store.mjs, which imports them and keeps exporting APPROVAL_DECISIONS. The derivation of conflicts (analyseApprovals, _derive) stays in project-store.mjs and is not part of this module; the approvals map is what a later reader would pass to it. The notices come in this order: torn_last_line first, then unreadable_last_line and malformed_record in line order, then approval_unusable in record order, which is the order of the store's recovered list today (source: unusableApproval and ProjectStore#_replay in project-store.mjs)

schemaVerdict(version, { supported, migrate }) is the refusal policy both callers share, and the only place its texts live. version is the schema_version the caller read from meta.json, or supported when there is no meta.json or its schema_version key is absent; a key that is present is passed as it is, null included. It returns { ok: true, migrate: false } when version equals supported; { ok: true, migrate: true } when version is lower and migrate is true (the store); and otherwise { ok: false, code, message } with code in REPLAY_REFUSALS: 'future_schema' when version is higher, 'needs_migration' when version is lower and migrate is not true (the reader), and 'bad_schema_version' when version is not a whole number of 1 or more (DEVIATION C, its own criterion, WP19-04 AC14 and WP19-05 AC07). What is pinned is the code and what the message must say, not the exact sentence: the code 'needs_migration' and a message that names the remedy (matching /any daemon command that opens the store migrates it/) and says the reader writes nothing (matching /this reader writes nothing/); the code 'future_schema' and a message that names the version found and the version supported and says the found one is newer (matching /newer/). The wording of pull request #365 at its commit 094970a (red at 58b4e97) is the starting text: 'schema version <v> is older than <supported>: any daemon command that opens the store migrates it, and this reader writes nothing, so it cannot read it until then'. The criteria use the two regular expressions above, so a later rewording that keeps both statements passes. Migration itself, and the choice to write, stay in the store (source: ProjectStore#open in project-store.mjs; Vault#tasksReader in pull request #365)

the function is pure: it reads and writes no file, no network, no clock and no source of randomness, makes no timer, reads no host global but the language's own built-ins and TextDecoder (the one host global it may use, constructed with fatal true, to decode a line of bytes), never changes its inputs, and returns a state that shares nothing with a second call's. It names no ProjectStore, projectStore(, coordinator( or new Coordinator, because requirement 3 of SO-1.01 (test 'SO-1.01 req 3' in test/project-wiring.test.mjs, which is not changed) lets only the vault, the coordinator and the project store name them (source: contracts/scope-one/specs/SO-1.01-canonical-execution-integration.json; test/project-wiring.test.mjs; the review of PG-W-21A, where purity checked only by grep was bypassed)

fixed id sets: every notice code is in the frozen REPLAY_NOTICES (torn_last_line, unreadable_last_line, malformed_record, approval_unusable) and every refusal code in the frozen REPLAY_REFUSALS (future_schema, needs_migration, bad_schema_version, unreadable_middle_line, non_record_line); the module writes no code of its own where it returns one (source: the review of PG-W-21A, fixed rule ids)

out of scope for this task, by design: the store and the reader calling it (WP19-05), any change to the write path (append, _appendLocked, _record, locking), to compact, to migration and to the derivation of conflicts, a lock-free read mode that opens the store, and a reader for view('task') or conflicts(), which will call this function later and has its own contract; nothing here decides ADR 8 or anything in trust governance
tasks.description: Repo: memev. The project store replays its event log (ProjectStore#_replay and #_applyRecord in src/engine/project-store.mjs), and the read-only reader that pull request #365 adds (Vault#tasksReader in src/engine/vault.mjs, PG-19.2) replays it again by its own copy of the rules, held to the store only by tests. This task extracts the rules into one pure module with no import, src/engine/project-replay.mjs, and tests every rule on its own. It writes the module and its tests; the callers are moved onto it in WP19-05. The state it returns is by kind and id, plus what the store keeps beside it (the sequence, the generation, the used ids, the keys, the sources, the approval events and the highest clock), so that the store can use the same function and not a reduced one. The tests live in test/project-replay.test.mjs and import the not-yet-existing module with a dynamic import inside a try, so a missing module is an assertion failure and never a load error. The ordering in the repository is fixed by the owner of the review: pull request #365 lands first, with its copy and its agreement test, and this contract then moves both callers onto the shared function.

criteria.statement: the module exists and exports exactly REPLAY_NOTICES, REPLAY_REFUSALS, APPROVAL_DECISIONS, unusableApproval, createReplayState, applyRecord, replayLog and schemaVerdict: the three functions that replay and check are functions, the three sets are frozen lists with exactly the codes named in the requirements, and the module has no other export; each test first asserts that the import succeeded and that the export it uses is the right type, so the red run fails on those assertions

tasks.title: The project store and the read-only reader both replay through the shared function, and agree on one fixed log, over a reopen and with a torn last line, with the facade, the disk test and the wiring rule unchanged
requirements: SR-1.15: no code without a caller (source: docs/scope-one/WBS.md leaf 2.2.15; owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)

ProjectStore#_replay in src/engine/project-store.mjs calls replayLog(the bytes of the log, { truncate: true }), throws a ProjectStoreError with the code and message of state.refusal when the replay refuses the log, writes nothing in that case, and ProjectStore#_applyRecord calls applyRecord, and neither keeps its own copy of the apply rules or of the line splitting. What stays in the store: the reset of its fields, the read of the file, the cut of the file at cut.keep_bytes (a write, kept in the store), the set of the store's own fields (seq, generation, entities, eventKeys, usedIds, sources, approvals, clock, recovered) from the state, the derivation of conflicts (_derive and analyseApprovals), the rewrite of every snapshot in open(), the lock, and the migration. The store's observable fields keep their names and values, and each message of recovered keeps its text. ProjectStore#open() takes the verdict of schemaVerdict(version, { supported: SCHEMA_VERSION, migrate: true }) and throws a ProjectStoreError with its code and message (source: ProjectStore#open, #_replay and #_applyRecord in project-store.mjs)

Vault#tasksReader(identity, project) in src/engine/vault.mjs (added by pull request #365, signed as PG-19.2) calls replayLog(the bytes of the log, { truncate: false }), throws a VaultError with the code and message of state.refusal when the replay refuses the log (the same codes and messages as the store's), and calls schemaVerdict(version, { supported: SCHEMA_VERSION, migrate: false }) and holds no apply rule of its own; its body no longer contains a JSON.parse, a split of the log or a test of a refused record. It still needs a credential that may read; returns null for a project that has neither a meta.json nor an event log (and creates nothing); returns an empty reader for a project that has a meta.json and no log; refuses a project whose schema version is above the supported one with future_schema and one below it with needs_migration, with the messages of schemaVerdict (the codes and the pinned phrases of WP19-04, not one fixed sentence), as a VaultError; does not apply an unterminated last line and does not cut it; takes no lock; and does not open the store, directly or by any other route: its body holds none of ProjectStore, projectStore, new ProjectStore or .open( (source: pull request #365, Vault#tasksReader and its tests; PG-19.2)

the facade is unchanged and stays silent: Vault#tasksReader returns a frozen object whose only member is snapshot(kind), also frozen, which returns structuredClone copies of the records of that kind as a plain object; it has no write method and no way to reach a ProjectStore. The reader surfaces no notice: no member, no field of what snapshot returns, and no output to the console or to a stream; the shared function returns the notices, the reader drops them, and where they should show (a count, a log line, a field) is left to a later spec, which must change the facade's test on purpose. The tests of PG-19.2 for it, WP19-03 AC01 to AC06 in test/cli-work.test.mjs, including the agreement test on one fixed log with a repeated id, a refused stale-generation record, a tombstone, approvals, a record with no entity and a line that is not JSON in the middle, compared with the store on a copy for every kind the store declares, pass unchanged, and test/cli-work.test.mjs is byte-unchanged; the one exception is made only if deviation D is signed (an unreadable middle line then refuses the log, so the fixed log's line that is not JSON, and the record after it, move out of the agreement log into a test of the refusal, and nothing else in that file changes; WP19-05 AC10 and the limited-diff criterion below) (source: contracts/programme/specs/PG-19.2-memev-work-command-wired-to-runwork.json, WP19-03)

the agreement is tested again here, over a reopen: one fixed log of the same shapes is replayed through the reader and through the store opened on a copy of the project directory, for every declared kind, then the store and the vault are closed and opened again and both agree again, then more records are appended through the store and a new reader agrees with the store again; and a log with a torn last line, a whole last record with no newline and a multi-byte character before it gives the same records through both, the reader leaves the file's bytes as they were, and the store leaves a file whose every line parses and whose size is the keep_bytes of the replay (source: pull request #365, the agreement test; the byte count fix of WP19-04)

carried over from PG-19.2, unchanged and checked again: test/project-wiring.test.mjs is byte-unchanged and passes (SO-1.01 requirement 3); src/cli/work-store.mjs calls Vault#tasksReader and contains none of ProjectStore, projectStore, project-store or Coordinator; test/cli-work-e2e.test.mjs does not contain runWork or openStore and is byte-unchanged; its disk test, which takes the size, mtime, sha256 and folder list of every file under the vault root and the config folder before and after `memev work impact` beside a running daemon, still shows no file added, removed or changed, and the daemon stays healthy (source: pull request #365, the e2e test; contracts/programme/specs/PG-19.2-memev-work-command-wired-to-runwork.json)

the reader is a point-in-time view and not a live one: Vault#tasksReader() replays the log once, when it is called; snapshot(kind) returns structuredClone copies of that state and reads no file again; a record appended afterwards, by the store or anything else, is not seen by that reader, and a new call to Vault#tasksReader() sees it; a copy that a caller changes does not change the next snapshot. The work command reads once per call (memev work impact is one-shot), so nothing in this contract makes the reader live (source: pull request #365, Vault#tasksReader and memev work impact; PG-19.2)

the reader does not open the store, even read-only: ProjectStore#open() rewrites every snapshot and cuts a torn last line and takes no lock, which beside a live daemon can change files and cut a line the daemon is still writing. A read mode that opens the store without a write would need its own contract and a proof, on disk beside a live daemon, that it changes nothing; this contract adds none (source: pull request #365, 'Why the reader does not open the store')

changes are limited to the store's replay and the reader's body: src/engine/project-store.mjs changes only _replay, _applyRecord, the import of the shared module, open() (for the verdict) and the removal of unusableApproval and APPROVAL_DECISIONS, which move to the shared module (APPROVAL_DECISIONS stays exported from project-store.mjs); src/engine/vault.mjs changes only the body of Vault#tasksReader and one added import line; no other src file changes; the write path, locking, snapshots, migration, derivation and every other method of both files are untouched. src/cli, src/engine/coordinator.mjs, src/engine/project-state.mjs, docs/schemas/, test/project-wiring.test.mjs, test/cli-work.test.mjs, test/cli-work-e2e.test.mjs, contracts/ and docs/scope-one/ are not changed; test/project-store.test.mjs and test/cli-work.test.mjs change only where they assert that a bad line in the middle is skipped, and only if deviation D is signed (source: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026)
